newsitem.title: USA: "Men in Black" tops U.S. box office sales again.
newsitem.headline: "Men in Black" tops U.S. box office sales again.

text.p: "Men In Black" became the third movie of 1997 to top box-office ticket sales for three straight weekends as it fended off two strong new entries, studio estimates said Sunday.
The alien sleuth comedy, starring Will Smith and Tommy Lee Jones, earned about $19 million for the weekend, a 37 percent drop from the previous weekend, bringing its total so far to $172.1 million.

"George of the Jungle," a live-action remake of the 1960s animated television series, opened in second place with $16.3 million in ticket sales. Since its Wednesday release, the movie, starring Brendan Fraser, has earned about $22.7 million. For the three days, it averaged $6,504 from 2,506 screens.
The Jodie Foster sci-fi drama "Contact" slipped a notch to third with $16.1 million in ticket sales, bringing its 10-day total to $47.4 million. Its average of $7,338 was the highest in the top 10.
Debuting in fourth was "Nothing to Lose," a Martin Lawrence and Tim Robbins comedy, which earned $11.6 million. It averaged $6,230 from 1,862 screens. Both new entries are released by Walt Disney Co.

"George of the Jungle" saw a hefty 33 percent jump in business from Friday to Saturday, according to Phil Barlow, president of Disney's Buena Vista Pictures distribution unit. "We'd hoped that we would break through to a wider audience and we seem to be doing that already," Barlow told Reuters.
"This is a good start." The family movie was playing well with teenagers and young adults, he added.
"Face/Off," a thriller starring John Travolta and Nicolas Cage, fell two places to fifth with $9 million in sales, a 27 percent decline. Its four-week total stands at $86.4 million.
The other movies of 1997 to enjoy three-week runs atop the box office were the "Star Wars" reissue in January and February and Jim Carrey's "Liar Liar" in March and April.
"Men in Black" is expected to be ousted from the top spot next weekend when Harrison Ford's action drama "Air Force One" opens.

One other new entry, Jackie Chan's "Operation Condor," opened in eighth place with $4.7 million in sales and a $3,068 per screen average. The movie originally came out in 1991 as "Armor of God II: Operation Condor." Disney-owned Miramax Films reissued the movie with English overdubs and new sound and music.
"Men in Black" is released by Columbia Pictures, a unit of Sony Corp. The studio will also release "Air Force One."
"Contact" is released by Warner Bros, a unit of Time Warner Inc.
"Face/Off" is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.
